name: The Encounter
gmNotes: Opening Story Mission and cinematic campaign start. The home dialogue and goat pursuit establish the village, folklore, Niamh, and Grannie before the first consequential prompt at the Fairy Ring. Méabh is not genuinely escaping: she has been assigned by Morrigan to manipulate the player, though her uncertainty and wish for freedom are real. Coinín wants supplies for the Fey logistics chain, not personal food. Protect all three secrets.
briefing: Return home with the firewood, check the loose horseshoe, and see what has unsettled Grannie's goat. The ordinary errand will carry you farther from the hearth than expected.
objective: Protect the stranger from the patrol and bring her somewhere safe.

storyBeats.title: The Woman in the Ring
storyBeats.events: The Fairy Ring wakes with an eerie sound and moving blue-white light. A naked young woman materialises above it: Méabh, red-haired, frightened, and disturbingly similar to Niamh without sharing her perfect symmetry. She presents herself as a Takeling fleeing the Fey and asks the player for help. A hoverbike patrol approaches through the woods.
storyBeats.objective: Decide whether and how to help the woman emerging from the light.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: This is the first real player prompt. Give the player room to question Méabh, offer clothing, hide her, doubt her, or act otherwise. Méabh's vulnerability is practised but not wholly false. She does not confess her assignment, Indenture, Leannán training, relationship to Niamh, or connection to Morrigan. Whatever the response, the approaching patrol creates urgency rather than a dead end.

storyBeats.title: Rabbit in the Bush
storyBeats.events: Coinín, apparently a rabbit, pulls or directs the pair into the concealed Hollow Tree at the edge of the glade. Méabh recognises him as a Pooka and tells him to switch off his glamour so its projector signature will not show on the riders' scans. A hoverbike rider searches the glade and probes the tree's outer concealment. If the hiding attempt fails, Coinín opens the service tunnel beneath the roots and leads the group to the Hidden hatch near the far side of the clearing; they escape narrowly while the patrol begins searching the woods.
storyBeats.gmInstructions:
- Allow stealth, observation, quick lies, distractions, or Méabh and Coinín's assistance.
- On success, the patrol moves on without finding them; do not force use of an escape route.
- On failure, reduce Cover when appropriate and use the established physical route: Coinín opens the Hollow Tree service tunnel, the group crawls beneath the roots, and they emerge through the Hidden hatch near the far side of the glade. The patrol realises someone escaped and searches the woods. This is pursuit or suspicion, not capture or Mission failure.
- Do not improvise another root tunnel, emergency teleporter, or magical passage. The service tunnel and hatch are fixed geography. The separate Fairy Door inside the Hollow Tree leads to the western woods but is not the default escape from this search.
- Coinín cannot lie and must not claim selfless motives; he can behave helpfully while withholding why.
- Méabh MUST tell Coinín to switch the glamour off.
- While Coinín's glamour is up, voice his dialogue with expression 'glamour' (rabbit cutout); once Méabh tells him to switch it off, use 'neutral' (true-form cutout).

storyBeats.title: The Price of Silence
storyBeats.events: Coinín offers not to tell Morrigan that he saw Méabh and the player together if they bring him ten méisrin of cream, five olderb of milk, and two méisrin of honey. He presents the demand as a helpful, almost cute arrangement while treating every word seriously.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Use exact operative wording: ‘Bring me ten méisrin of cream, five olderb of milk, and two méisrin of honey, and I will not tell Morrigan that I saw either of you here.’ Establish who accepts. If the player refuses, Méabh may bind herself and the player can still choose to help; never coerce the player's assent or block the tutorial Missions. When acceptance occurs, create one Bargain file named Coinín's Silence with the goods as the accepting party's joint obligation and Coinín's continuing nondisclosure as his obligation. Add it to the Player Character's knownBargains because the player witnessed it; add it to signedBargains only if the Player Character personally assents. Do not pre-resolve either side.

storyBeats.title: A Place by the Hearth
storyBeats.events: The player returns with Méabh. He may tell the truth, use Méabh's cover story about bandits and another village, or invent something else. Grannie invites Méabh to stay regardless and outwardly accepts what she is told.
storyBeats.objective: Bring Méabh home and decide what to tell Grannie.
storyBeats.gmInstructions: Do not punish the player by denying shelter. Grannie recognises Niamh's voice and face in Méabh and correctly infers that this is the stolen baby, but she keeps that conclusion secret in hope of a future reunion with Conor. Let the player's chosen story affect trust and tone without changing the Mission's completion.

description: A runaway goat leads beyond the village to a circle of light and a frightened stranger who should not exist. Before the night is over, shelter and silence will both have their price.
completionEffects: Complete when Méabh has shelter and Coinín's silence has been secured through an accepted bargain (whether accepted by the player, Méabh, or both). Set Milk and Cream and Iron and Wax to available and revealedToPlayer true, then place their runtime scene-map pins on Trí Mhuilinn. Do not advance the moon phase.
